comments.body:
# Provider capability matrix — OpenAI Responses API readiness (evidence, 2026-08-21)

Toolchain pinned by this checkout: **pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.2**, **openai SDK 2.53.0**. All
file:line citations are against worktree `work-b612` at `origin/main` (post-6fb4d801c9). Probe
transcripts were produced in this worktree's `.venv` interpreter.

## The matrix

Classification key: **Responses-ready** = a real `OpenAIResponsesModel` construction path exists
under the pin AND rebar could route to it after the (named) rebar-side unblocks;
**Chat-Completions-only** = the pin offers no Responses construction path for this row, so vendor
capability is moot for the migration; **UNKNOWN** = evidence missing, named per row.

| # | Endpoint / row | Status | Evidence (cited, not inferred) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hosted OpenAI via `openai:` / `openai-chat:` (no `base_url`; delegated to pydantic-ai `infer_provider`) | **Responses-ready** (rebar-blocked today — see constraints) | Probe: `infer_model("openai-responses:gpt-4o")` constructs `OpenAIResponsesModel` + `OpenAIProvider` under 1.107.2. Probe: `infer_model("openai:gpt-4o")` emits `PydanticAIDeprecationWarning`: "In v2.0, 'openai:' will resolve to the OpenAI Responses API by default." Contract tests (`tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py`) pass identically for structured-output, streaming, tool-call, 429-retry and base-URL routing under both prefixes against the two wire protocols. |
| 2 | Custom `base_url` OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LMStudio/Ollama/vLLM/LiteLLM recipe) via `ProviderSession._build_openai` | **Chat-Completions-only** (in rebar, by construction) | `providers.py:105-106`: the builder is registered only under `"openai"`/`"openai-chat"`; `providers.py:153`: the per-candidate endpoint interpose is keyed on the same two names. A `openai-responses:` string never reaches `_build_openai`, so `base_url` would be ignored → the row cannot be Responses-ready without a rebar change. Whether any given local server implements `/v1/responses` is a separate vendor question → see UNKNOWN row 8. |
| 3 | Per-candidate `endpoint` override (fallback chains, task cc33, `ProviderSession.model_for`) | **Chat-Completions-only** (same keying) | `providers.py:150-155`: `endpoint_override` registers `_build_openai` only for `{"openai", "openai-chat"}`. |
| 4 | `gateway/openai:` (Pydantic AI Gateway) | **Chat-Completions-only** under the pin | Probe: `infer_model("gateway/openai:gpt-4o")` (with `PYDANTIC_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL` set) constructs `OpenAIChatModel`. 1.107.2 exposes no `gateway/openai-responses` prefix in `known_model_names()`. |
| 5 | `deepseek:` | **Chat-Completions-only** under the pin | Probe: constructs `OpenAIChatModel` + `DeepSeekProvider`. No Responses construction path exists for the prefix in 1.107.2. |
| 6 | `grok:`, `moonshotai:`, `heroku:` | **Chat-Completions-only** under the pin | Probe: each constructs `OpenAIChatModel` (+ `GrokProvider`/`MoonshotAIProvider`/`HerokuProvider`). Same reasoning as row 5. |
| 7 | `cerebras:` | **Chat-Completions-only** under the pin | Probe: constructs `CerebrasModel`, which 1.107.2 implements as an OpenAI-chat-protocol model; no Responses path for the prefix. |
| 8 | `xai:`, `groq:` | **UNKNOWN (construction untestable here)** | Probe: both raise `ImportError` — the `xai-sdk` / `groq` optional packages are not installed in this checkout and are not in rebar's extras (`pyproject.toml` ships only `[openai]`, `[bedrock]`, `[google]`). Missing evidence: the constructed model class under those extras. Note `groq:` uses `GroqModel` (its own protocol), and `xai:` the xai-sdk — neither plausibly OpenAI-Responses, but that is inference, so the row stays UNKNOWN. |
| 9 | Vendor-side native `/v1/responses` support (DeepSeek, Groq, xAI, Cerebras, Moonshot, Heroku, LMStudio, Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM) | **UNKNOWN — and moot for 155c under the pin** | Missing evidence: vendor API documentation for each. Deliberately not researched: pydantic-ai 1.107.2 offers no third-party Responses construction path (rows 4-8), so vendor capability cannot change the migration decision until upstream adds one. Recorded so a future pin bump knows to re-ask. |

## Production-construction constraints (the `155c` edit-set, cited)

Four rebar code sites make `openai-responses:` unusable today even though pydantic-ai itself
constructs it (each verified by probe in this worktree):

1. **`src/rebar/llm/config.py:210-236` — `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` lacks `openai-responses`.**
   Probe: `split_provider_qualifier("openai-responses:gpt-4o")` → `(None, 'openai-responses:gpt-4o')`
   — the string is treated as an unqualified bare model name, so provider inference fails.
2. **`src/rebar/llm/providers.py` (`_pydantic_ai_known_providers`) — derived from
   `known_model_names()`, which has NO `openai-responses:` entries in 1.107.2** (probe: `False`),
   so `ProviderSession.is_resolvable("openai-responses")` → `False`, and `runner.py:406-411`
   then routes to `provider_factory(_provider_name)`, which "always raises `LLMConfigError`".
   Net effect: `model = "openai-responses:gpt-4o"` is a hard config error in rebar's runner,
   not a lazy delegation — even though bare `pydantic_ai.models.infer_model` accepts it.
   (Upstream's `infer_provider` special-cases the name the same way it does the deprecated
   `google-gla` aliases rebar already compensates for via `_DEPRECATED_PROVIDER_ALIASES`.)
3. **`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:417-425` — `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` has no `openai-responses`
   key.** Probe: `capabilities_for("openai-responses:gpt-4o")` degrades to
   `native_structured_output=False` (vs `True` for `openai-chat:gpt-4o`) — a silent
   structured-output downgrade (PromptedOutput instead of NativeOutput) if resolution were
   fixed without this map.
4. **The `openai:` → `openai-chat:` normalizers hard-code the Chat pin:**
   `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:199-200` (`_pai_model`) and
   `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:246-269` (`_resolve_target`, which also unifies the
   `openai`/`openai-chat` qualifier family). A default flip must revisit both, or `openai:`
   strings will keep resolving to Chat regardless of any new default.

Also relevant for 155c: `ProviderSession._build_openai`'s `_RebarOpenAICompatibleProvider`
withdraws `supports_json_schema_output` for opaque base_url endpoints (providers.py, story S4
AC5) — a Responses-capable custom endpoint would need an equivalent decision, since the
Responses API's structured-output path differs.

## Behavioural diff instrument

`tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py` (landed with this ticket) parameterizes identical
assertions over `openai-chat:` / `openai-responses:` — construction dispatch, custom-base-URL
routing (`/v1/chat/completions` vs `/v1/responses`), structured output, streaming, tool calls,
and the 429 retry surface. Current diff result: **all 12 cases pass under both prefixes**; the
one measured invariant worth naming is that the retry lives in the openai SDK
(`AsyncOpenAI` `max_retries=2` → exactly 3 wire requests before `ModelHTTPError(429)`) and is
identical across both APIs. Re-run after any pin bump: `pytest tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py`.

## Completion summary

- Capability matrix + production-construction constraints: previous comment (9 rows, each cited; UNKNOWN rows name the missing evidence — xai:/groq: construction under absent extras, vendor-side /v1/responses support).
- Contract tests landed via Gerrit change 2081 (merged; Verified+1 = CI green on py3.11/3.12/3.13 Linux + macOS, LLM-Review+1): tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py, commit 4a6b4e266b7. 12 cases, parameterized [chat]/[responses] — real infer_model construction, structured output, streaming, tool calls, 429 retry surface, custom-base-URL routing. All pass under BOTH prefixes; the parametrize ids are the migration's behavioural-diff instrument.
- make lint and make typecheck pass in this worktree. make test: the FULL suite ran green in CI on the exact patchset (the Verified lane runs the same suite). A first local full run failed 27 tests, all proven ENVIRONMENTAL, not repository evidence: this harness injects safe.bareRepository=explicit via GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE env vars, which breaks every bare-repo-fixture test ('fatal: cannot use bare repository … safe.bareRepository is explicit'); rerunning every failing file with those vars unset passes (44/44 + 47/47). A sanitized full local run is in progress and green so far.
- Verdict for 155c (upbeat-illadvised-springtail): hosted OpenAI is Responses-ready at the pydantic-ai layer; everything else is Chat-Completions-only or UNKNOWN under the 1.107.2 pin. The migration's edit-set is the four constraint sites named in the matrix comment (config.py KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES, providers.py is_resolvable/_pydantic_ai_known_providers, capabilities.py _PROFILE_RESOLVERS, the openai:→openai-chat: normalizers).

## Context
Split from `upbeat-illadvised-springtail` (155c-218b-c128-4700) per operator decision 2026-08-19.
That ticket originally carried BOTH the research (which endpoints can move) and the change (moving
them). The research must not sit behind the migration's acceptance criteria, so it is filed here
and springtail is blocked by it.

Pydantic AI v2 makes the Responses API the default for `openai:` (the pinned 1.107.2 already
emits a `PydanticAIDeprecationWarning` saying so on every `openai:` construction). rebar
currently pins Chat Completions explicitly via the `openai-chat:` prefix (the deprecation repair
on `dragonish-sylphic-sheep`). rebar should migrate deliberately, after proving compatibility,
rather than inherit the semantic change implicitly.

## Scope — evidence only, no migration
This ticket does NOT flip any provider to `openai-responses:`. Its product is (a) the capability
matrix + production-construction constraints, recorded as a comment on this ticket, and (b) the
contract tests that will later prove the migration safe.

Edit-set: ONE new file, `tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py`. No `src/rebar` change —
findings about the runtime are recorded on this ticket for `155c` to act on, not patched here.

## Approach
Two evidence layers, both against the pinned toolchain (pydantic-ai 1.107.2, this checkout):

1. **Static + probe inventory** of rebar's OpenAI-compatible surface. The rows are exactly the
   OpenAI-compatible names rebar admits: (i) hosted `openai:` / `openai-chat:` (delegated to
   pydantic-ai `infer_provider` when no `base_url`), (ii) the custom `base_url` builder
   `ProviderSession._build_openai` (LMStudio/Ollama/vLLM/LiteLLM recipe, story S4), (iii) the
   per-candidate `endpoint` override (`ProviderSession.model_for`, task cc33),
   (iv) `gateway/openai`, and (v) the OpenAI-compatible vendor qualifiers in
   `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` (`deepseek`, `grok`, `xai`, `groq`, `cerebras`, `moonshotai`,
   `heroku`). Each row is classified Responses-ready / Chat-Completions-only / UNKNOWN from
   cited evidence: rebar source (file:line), pinned pydantic-ai source/behaviour (which model
   class `infer_model` constructs per prefix, verified by probe), and live interpreter probes
   run in this worktree. Vendor-side questions that the pin already decides (pydantic-ai offers
   no Responses construction path for third-party prefixes) are classified from the pin;
   anything requiring off-toolchain evidence (e.g. whether a vendor's own API implements
   `/v1/responses`) is recorded UNKNOWN with the missing evidence named.
2. **Contract tests** in `tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py`: a stub
   OpenAI-compatible server behind `httpx.MockTransport` that speaks BOTH wire protocols
   (`/chat/completions` and `/responses`). Injection mechanism, stated concretely because the
   `monkeypatch.setattr(httpx, "AsyncHTTPTransport", ...)` seam of
   `test_openai_compatible_provider.py` does NOT reach stock pydantic-ai construction
   (`create_async_http_client()` builds a bare `AsyncClient`; providers.py:277-283): the test
   builds one explicit production `OpenAIProvider(base_url=<stub url>, api_key="test",
   http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler)))` and hands it to
   `pydantic_ai.models.infer_model(model_string, provider_factory=lambda name: provider)` —
   the SAME `provider_factory` hook rebar's own `ProviderSession` uses in production
   (providers.py `model_for`), so `infer_model` still performs the real prefix→model-class
   dispatch and genuinely constructs `OpenAIChatModel` / `OpenAIResponsesModel`; only the
   socket inside the explicitly-passed client is faked, and no module attribute is
   monkeypatched. Tests are parameterized over
   the two prefixes (`openai-chat:` / `openai-responses:`) so the identical assertions run
   against both and the parametrize ids ARE the behavioural diff for `155c`. Assertions cover:
   structured output (Agent `output_type` round-trip), streaming (`run_stream` issues a
   streaming request and yields text), tool calls (a tool-call turn then a final turn), retry
   behaviour — scoped precisely to what the mechanism exercises: a 429 from the stub surfaces
   as `ModelHTTPError` under BOTH prefixes, pinning pydantic-ai's default (no hidden
   model-layer retry) 429 surface across the two APIs; this is deliberately NOT a claim about
   `ProviderSession._build_openai`'s transport, which the test does not construct (that
   builder cannot build `openai-responses:` at all today — recorded as a constraint in the
   matrix comment with its providers.py citation, not tested here) — and custom-base-URL routing (requests hit the stub `base_url` at the API-specific
   path).

Also recorded on the ticket (the production-construction constraints for `155c`): the four
places that today make `openai-responses:` unusable in rebar even though pydantic-ai itself
constructs it — `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` (src/rebar/llm/config.py) lacks `openai-responses`, so
`split_provider_qualifier` treats the string as unqualified; `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()`
(src/rebar/llm/providers.py) derives from `known_model_names()`, which has no
`openai-responses:` entries, so `is_resolvable` is False and `runner.run()` raises
`LLMConfigError` (src/rebar/llm/runner.py, the `provider_factory` else-branch);
`_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` (src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py) has no `openai-responses` key, so
capability resolution degrades (`native_structured_output=False`); and the `openai:` →
`openai-chat:` normalizers (`_pai_model` in src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py and
`model_classes._resolve_target`) hard-code the Chat pin. Default assumption: these are
`155c`'s edit-set, not this ticket's.

## Testing
The deliverable IS tests. Happy path: every parameterized case passes against the stub for both
prefixes where behaviour is common. Failure/edge path: the 429-retry case asserts the error
surface, and the structured-output case asserts the parse of a well-formed body (the stub also
lets a later behavioural-diff run mark genuinely divergent cases per-API). Verified by
`.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py` plus full `make test`,
`make lint`, `make typecheck` in this worktree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [non-codebase] A capability-matrix comment on this ticket classifies every row of rebar's
      OpenAI-compatible surface (hosted openai/openai-chat, custom base_url builder,
      per-candidate endpoint override, gateway/openai, deepseek, grok, xai, groq, cerebras,
      moonshotai, heroku) as Responses-ready, Chat-Completions-only, or UNKNOWN, each row with
      a cited source (rebar file:line, pinned pydantic-ai behaviour, or probe transcript) —
      checked by reading the comment.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The same comment records the production-construction constraints: each rebar code site
      that blocks `openai-responses:` today, with file:line — checked by reading the comment
      against the named sites.
- [ ] Contract tests exist at `tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py`, construct REAL
      pydantic-ai models (no mocks of construction; only the transport is stubbed), and assert
      structured-output, streaming, tool-call, retry, and custom-base-URL behaviour — checked
      by reading the test file and running it.
- [ ] The tests are parameterized over `openai-chat:` and `openai-responses:` so re-running
      them produces a per-case behavioural diff — checked by the parametrize ids in
      `pytest --collect-only` output.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Any endpoint whose status cannot be established from evidence is recorded
      UNKNOWN with the specific missing evidence named — checked by reading the matrix comment.
- [ ] `make test`, `make lint`, `make typecheck` pass in this worktree — checked by running
      them.
